facts: Ramsey asks people to write a monthly budget before the month begins.
It is zero-based: income minus planned spending equals zero.
Every dollar is assigned a job: rent, food, transport, debt payment, savings.
He asks people to give every dollar a purpose instead of wondering where it went.
For categories that leak, he recommends cash in envelopes, one per category.
When the envelope is empty, spending in that category stops.
The book's subtitle is 'A Proven Plan for Financial Fitness': Ramsey frames money like physical fitness, where doing the routine matters more than knowing the theory.
Ramsey lays out his plan as seven baby steps: the starter fund of $1,000 comes first, the debt snowball second, a full emergency fund of three to six months of expenses third.
Ramsey asks couples to write the budget together each month, so both agree on where the money goes.
scene_details: A written budget with one line per category
Cash envelopes, one for each category
An empty envelope before month end
A couple sitting down with the written budget
tension: Most people cannot say where last month's money went, yet they feel a budget will cage them.
opening_idea: Start with the empty envelope in the last week of the month.

lessons.idea: Decide where money goes before you have it, so spending becomes a set of choices.
lessons.anchor: In Ramsey's zero-based budget every dollar has a job before the month starts, and an empty envelope ends that category.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A parent who sets a fixed pizza-night amount at the start of the month and knows exactly when it ends.

reflect_final: Which category of your spending would surprise you most if you wrote down last month's actual total today?

use_cases.situation: You and your partner argue about spending.
use_cases.move: Sit down before the month starts and give each expected sum a job; extras need an agreed line.

use_cases.situation: A friend suggests a pricey trip.
use_cases.move: Say: I have a line for that, let me check what is left in it.

use_cases.situation: It is the last day of the month.
use_cases.move: Write each category's real total beside its planned total and note the biggest gap.

pocket_idea: In Ramsey's budget every dollar has a job before the month starts; write next month's lines before the first payday.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Ramsey's budget ends with zero left over, because every dollar already has a job.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Dave Ramsey's budget is written before the month starts. Income minus planned spending equals zero, so every dollar has a job: rent, food, debt, savings. For categories that leak, he suggests cash in an envelope, and when it is empty that spending stops.
